headline: Large User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill requires large energy users, like data centers, to pay for the costs of increasing electric generating capacity, shifting these costs away from residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, U.S. Sen. Mark Warner, consumer advocacy and utility watchdog organizations.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial users, Data Center Coalition.
news_headline: Warner Backs Bill to Shift Data Center Costs Away from Ratepayers
news_summary: U.S. Sen. Mark Warner co-sponsored federal legislation, the "Power for the People Act," aimed at making data center operators bear more of the costs associated with their significant energy demands and infrastructure upgrades. This aligns with Virginia's HB 1393, which directs the State Corporation Commission to establish rates for large energy users (25 MW or more) to recover costs of increasing electric generating capacity.

headline: Data Center Water Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates water users providing water to data centers to report monthly on the total volume of potable and reclaimed water consumed, increasing transparency on water usage.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservation advocates, Sen. Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: Virginia to Require More Detailed Water Use Reporting for Data Centers Beginning in 2027
news_summary: Virginia has approved legislation, identical to SB 553, that will require more detailed reporting of water usage by data centers and other major customer categories, effective January 1, 2027. This aims to provide transparency on water consumption amidst the rapid growth of the data center industry in the state.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise
short_summary: This bill establishes regulations for data center siting, including requirements for site assessments and noise studies, and sets limits on noise levels to address community concerns.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residential groups, environmental advocates, Del. Joshua Thomas, Del. Sam Rasoul.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry, Data Center Coalition.
news_headline: Virginia has a new two-year budget. Here's what lawmakers now require of data centers.
news_summary: Virginia's new budget includes mandates for the Department of Environmental Quality to regulate data centers' noise levels, with standards to be set by 2029 and fines for violations starting in 2030. This addresses rising concerns from residents about noise pollution from these facilities.
